slides.title: Personalized Restaurant Ordering System
slides.audience_question: What is the project, who is it for, and what is its technical focus?
slides.message: A lightweight, explainable, mobile-first ordering prototype for small restaurants.
slides.notes: Introduce the QR-based customer journey and the three recommendation signals in under 40 seconds.

content_relationship_brief.audience_question: What was built and why is the delivery model appropriate for a small restaurant?
content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: A mobile-first Rust web prototype connects QR ordering with explainable personalized recommendations.
content_relationship_brief.core_content_relation: Project identity, customer usage context and recommendation scope
content_relationship_brief.evidence_and_source_responsibility: The mobile menu visual proves the product form; the subtitle and mechanism line define the research boundary.
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: No fixed left-right template; the image model chooses a clear academic cover composition.

visual_director_decision.page_intent: Make supervisors immediately understand that this is a working software-research prototype for phone-based restaurant ordering.
visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Use a real mobile ordering interface as product evidence and connect it visually to concise preference and co-order signals.
visual_director_decision.visual_metaphor: A restrained signal-to-menu connection, not a decorative technology metaphor.
visual_director_decision.focus_decision: Project title and the authentic phone menu experience share the visual focus.
visual_director_decision.layout_boundary: The image model controls composition; preserve generous margins and all locked text.

graphic_language_hint.suggested_graphic_language: Product-system cover using an authentic mobile UI, minimal signal annotations and an academic title system
graphic_language_hint.decision_source: Project positioning and mobile QR use case
graphic_language_hint.design_freedom: Composition may be asymmetric or layered if hierarchy stays clear and credible.

content_blocks.name: Positioning
content: Lightweight, explainable recommendations for small restaurants

must_keep: Lightweight, explainable recommendations for small restaurants
hard_boundaries: do not invent data or citations
image_prompt_constraints.quality: A real academic FYP defense cover with product evidence, not a restaurant advertisement.

slides.title: Problem and Research Gap
slides.audience_question: Why does a small restaurant need a different recommendation approach?
slides.message: Limited data, customer cold start, hard restrictions and weak transparency make conventional recommendation assumptions unsuitable.
slides.source_status: FYP report Sections 1.1–1.2; literature citations retained from report

content_relationship_brief.audience_question: What practical and research gap is addressed?
content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: A single restaurant needs lightweight personalisation that works before rich behavioural data exists.
content_relationship_brief.core_content_relation: Four constraints leading to one design response
content_relationship_brief.evidence_and_source_responsibility: Report-backed constraints motivate deterministic hybrid design without claiming commercial outcomes.
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: Use an evidence-led problem structure rather than a fixed card grid.

visual_director_decision.page_intent: Make the gap feel specific to a small restaurant, not a generic AI problem.
visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Organise the four constraints around the missing capability and end with the required system response.
visual_director_decision.visual_metaphor: A sparse-evidence funnel may be used lightly.
visual_director_decision.focus_decision: The four constraints converging on the research gap.
visual_director_decision.layout_boundary: No fixed layout; preserve clear reading order.

graphic_language_hint.suggested_graphic_language: Research-gap map with sparse-data cues and a concise design-response statement

content_blocks.name: Boundary
content: The study evaluates observable recommendation behaviour, not customer satisfaction or sales.

image_prompt_constraints.quality: Academic problem-framing page in the confirmed visual system.

slides.title: Research Questions and Objectives
slides.message: Three observable questions align preference impact, co-order impact and method comparison with build, recommend and evaluate objectives.

content_relationship_brief.audience_question: How are the research questions connected to the objectives?
content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: Each RQ has a controlled evaluation path within a complete web artefact.
content_relationship_brief.evidence_and_source_responsibility: Exact research scope comes from the report.
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: Use an alignment structure, not a text-heavy list.

visual_director_decision.page_intent: Give supervisors a compact mental model for the remainder of the presentation.
visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Pair each RQ with its observable output and group objectives into Build, Recommend and Evaluate.
visual_director_decision.focus_decision: Three RQ lanes with measurable outputs.
visual_director_decision.layout_boundary: Keep exact meaning while shortening only for slide readability.

graphic_language_hint.suggested_graphic_language: Research alignment matrix or three-lane logic map

content_blocks.name: RQ1
content: How do liked and disliked ingredients affect ranking and restriction compliance?

content_blocks.name: RQ2
content: How does increasing co-order evidence affect association measures and ranking?

content_blocks.name: RQ3
content: How do ingredient-only, co-order-only and hybrid methods recover a hidden dish?

slides.title: Proposed System and User Journey
slides.audience_question: How does the recommendation system fit into a real ordering journey?
slides.message: Customer actions, staff processing and completed orders form a closed learning loop.
slides.source_status: FYP report scope and implemented workflows

content_relationship_brief.audience_question: Who does what, and where does recommendation evidence enter?
content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: The web system turns QR access into an order and then converts completion into future behavioural evidence.
content_relationship_brief.core_content_relation: Dual-role journey plus learning feedback loop
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: Use a journey or sequence, not fixed cards.

visual_director_decision.page_intent: Show that recommendation is part of a complete system rather than an isolated algorithm.
visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Trace customer and staff actions across one ordered path, with completion feeding historical evidence.
aesthetic_risk_focus: making persistence look like autonomous ML
visual_director_decision.layout_boundary: Keep roles visually distinct and feedback explicit.

graphic_language_hint.suggested_graphic_language: Dual-lane user journey with one feedback loop
graphic_language_hint.design_freedom: Use clear role markers and a mobile touchpoint.

content_blocks.name: Learning loop
content: Completed basket → historical orders → popularity & co-order evidence

content_blocks.name: Boundary
content: Prototype checkout; no online payment processing

image_prompt_constraints.quality: Real software journey page in the confirmed visual system.

slides.title: Lightweight Web Architecture
slides.audience_question: How is the system structured for low coupling and small operational cost?
slides.message: One Rust/Axum process separates browser presentation, application services, recommendation logic and local persistence.

content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: Clear boundaries keep HTTP, scoring, persistence and presentation independent within a lightweight deployment.
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: Use an architecture graph without forcing equal boxes.

visual_director_decision.page_intent: Demonstrate engineering coherence and explain why the design is lightweight.
visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Show request flow through layers while naming focused module responsibilities.
visual_director_decision.focus_decision: Rust/Axum application as the orchestrating layer, not a monolith.

graphic_language_hint.suggested_graphic_language: Layered software architecture with module ownership labels

content_blocks.name: Runtime boundary
content: No external ML service or image host at runtime

must_keep: No external ML service at runtime
image_prompt_constraints.quality: Senior software architecture slide, not cloud marketing art.

slides.title: Recommendation Processing Pipeline
slides.message: Hard exclusions protect restrictions first; eligible dishes are then scored, adaptively combined, reranked and explained.
slides.source_status: FYP report recommendation design and implementation

content_relationship_brief.audience_question: What is the order of operations and why does it matter?
content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: Eligibility is separated from ranking so a popular dish can never override a disliked ingredient.
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: Use a readable process flow, not a crowded formula sheet.

visual_director_decision.page_intent: Make the algorithm understandable without code.
visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Show transformations from customer/context inputs to ranked explainable output, highlighting the hard gate.

graphic_language_hint.suggested_graphic_language: Data-analysis pipeline with a visually distinct hard eligibility gate
graphic_language_hint.design_freedom: Allow branch/merge where component signals combine.

image_prompt_constraints.quality: Clear method pipeline in the confirmed academic system.

slides.title: Explainability and Evidence Confidence
slides.audience_question: What does the user learn beyond the final rank?
slides.message: Every recommendation exposes the contributing signals, while evidence confidence describes support strength—not purchase probability.

content_relationship_brief.audience_question: How are reasons generated and interpreted safely?
content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: Reasons are assembled from inspectable evidence rather than vague algorithm labels.
content_relationship_brief.evidence_and_source_responsibility: Example wording must reflect real evidence types; confidence caveat prevents misinterpretation.
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: Use one evidence-rich example with annotations.

visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Deconstruct one recommendation reason into its evidence components and distinguish ranking score from confidence.
visual_director_decision.visual_metaphor: Evidence trace from signals to reason.
visual_director_decision.focus_decision: The plain-language reason and its traceable inputs.
visual_director_decision.layout_boundary: Keep the example readable at presentation distance.

graphic_language_hint.suggested_graphic_language: Annotated evidence trace around one recommendation result
graphic_language_hint.design_freedom: Use a reason sentence as the anchor.

content_blocks.name: Example reason
content: Recommended because it matches liked ingredients: chicken, chilli; matches preferred tag: spicy; and is often ordered with Nasi Lemak (D01).

content_blocks.name: Restriction
content: Disliked ingredients are excluded before ranking

content_blocks.name: Confidence boundary
content: Evidence confidence = amount and quality of supporting evidence
It is not the probability of purchase or liking

image_prompt_constraints.quality: Evidence explanation page, not generic AI trust marketing.

slides.title: Implemented System Outcomes
slides.audience_question: What can the working prototype actually do?
slides.message: The prototype connects customer ordering, explainable recommendations, staff operations and controlled evaluation in one web system.
slides.source_status: FYP report Chapter 4 and repository screenshots

content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: Both customer and administrator workflows are implemented and connected to the same recommendation and order state.
content_relationship_brief.core_content_relation: Two-role capability map around one shared system
content_relationship_brief.evidence_and_source_responsibility: Real screenshots prove implementation; labels summarise scope.
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: Use authentic interface evidence without creating a screenshot collage.

visual_director_decision.page_intent: Demonstrate implementation breadth while remaining coherent.
visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Use a small number of authentic interface views tied to four capability outcomes.
visual_director_decision.focus_decision: Connected customer mobile and admin workflow evidence.
visual_director_decision.layout_boundary: Prioritise readable interface crops and outcome labels.

slides.title: System Testing Results
slides.audience_question: Was the artefact tested across logic, workflow, security and responsive behaviour?
slides.message: All 115 Rust tests and all 55 selected report-level checks passed in the controlled local environment.

content_relationship_brief.audience_question: What was tested and what does a 100% pass rate mean?
content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: The tested requirements passed, but this does not establish production readiness or user satisfaction.
content_relationship_brief.core_content_relation: Quality gate, category breakdown and test boundary
content_relationship_brief.evidence_and_source_responsibility: Exact counts are report evidence; boundary limits interpretation.
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: Use a test evidence dashboard without commercial KPI styling.

visual_director_decision.page_intent: Show broad verification and honest scope.
visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Pair two headline test results with a category distribution and explicit environment boundary.
visual_director_decision.focus_decision: 115 passed and 55/55 passed as distinct measurements.

graphic_language_hint.suggested_graphic_language: Academic test summary with exact totals, compact breakdown and environment note
graphic_language_hint.design_freedom: Use bars, check matrix or other precise form.

content_blocks.name: Boundary
content: No load test or formal external usability study

slides.title: RQ1 & RQ2 — Observable Ranking Impact
slides.audience_question: Do explicit preferences and additional co-order evidence change recommendations as intended?
slides.message: Preferences changed eligibility and ranking immediately; stronger co-order evidence improved association strength and could move a candidate to rank 1.
slides.source_status: FYP report Sections 4.4.1–4.4.2 and evidence CSV files

content_relationship_brief.audience_question: What observable before/after changes answer RQ1 and RQ2?
content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: Hard exclusions are absolute, liked signals raise compatible dishes, and behavioural evidence can strengthen complementary ranking.
content_relationship_brief.core_content_relation: Before/after case evidence across two experiments
content_relationship_brief.evidence_and_source_responsibility: Rank changes are exact evidence; interpretation stays within selected scenarios.
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: Use a paired comparison without forcing symmetric card grids.

visual_director_decision.page_intent: Make preference and co-order effects concrete through memorable dish cases.
visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Use ranking trajectories and short evidence labels for RQ1 and RQ2.
visual_director_decision.focus_decision: Three large before/after changes, with D09 as an important no-movement nuance.
aesthetic_risk_focus: claiming every stronger association changes rank
visual_director_decision.layout_boundary: Keep case names, IDs and rank movements exact.

graphic_language_hint.suggested_graphic_language: Paired rank-movement evidence with explicit hard-exclusion marker
graphic_language_hint.design_freedom: Use slopes, arrows or rank strips.

slides.title: RQ3 — Recommendation Method Comparison
slides.audience_question: Which recommendation method recovered the hidden dish most reliably in the controlled test?
slides.message: Co-order-only and fixed hybrid achieved 100% Hit@3 across five cases; ingredient-only achieved 20%.
slides.notes: Explain the Hit@3 comparison, average ranks, why the co-order signal was strong, and the limits of a five-case fixed-profile test.
slides.source_status: Calculated from user report evidence and method-comparison CSV

content_relationship_brief.audience_question: How do the three methods compare, and how far can the result be generalised?
content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: Historical co-order evidence recovered all hidden dishes in Top 3 for this controlled sample, while the fixed ingredient profile recovered one.
content_relationship_brief.core_content_relation: Method comparison using Hit@3 and average hidden-dish rank, followed by interpretation and limitation
content_relationship_brief.evidence_and_source_responsibility: The chart carries the primary claim; average rank corroborates it; the experiment boundary prevents overclaiming.
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: Do not prescribe columns or cards; design a clear evidence-led academic result page.

visual_director_decision.page_intent: Let supervisors compare methods in seconds, then immediately see why the conclusion is bounded.
visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Make the three-method quantitative contrast the visual focus, supported by a compact case-level evidence trace and a visible limitation note.
visual_director_decision.visual_metaphor: No metaphor; use direct data structure.
visual_director_decision.focus_decision: The 20% / 100% / 100% Hit@3 contrast is the dominant focal point.
aesthetic_risk_focus: making hybrid appear statistically superior to co-order-only
visual_director_decision.layout_boundary: The image model controls chart composition; all labels, values and source text must remain readable.

graphic_language_hint.suggested_graphic_language: Direct comparison chart with exact values, compact evidence strip and explicit experiment-boundary annotation
graphic_language_hint.decision_source: Three-method metric comparison with a tied top result
graphic_language_hint.design_freedom: Use bars, lollipops or another precise comparison form; preserve exact values and tie.

content_blocks.name: Interpretation
content: Strong historical co-order evidence dominated these five hidden-dish cases.

slides.title: Contributions, Limitations and Future Work
slides.audience_question: What does the project contribute, and what remains unproven?
slides.message: The prototype establishes a lightweight, explainable system contribution; broader effectiveness requires real users, larger data and production infrastructure.

content_relationship_brief.audience_question: How should the result be interpreted responsibly?
content_relationship_brief.one_sentence_conclusion: Technical feasibility is demonstrated, but commercial and user outcomes are future research.
content_relationship_brief.evidence_and_source_responsibility: Claims are bounded by the report's explicit exclusions.
content_relationship_brief.layout_freedom: Use a progression or evidence boundary, not equal feature cards.

visual_director_decision.page_intent: Show maturity by balancing achievement with limitations.
visual_director_decision.expression_strategy: Connect each limitation to a concrete future action while preserving the project's contribution.
visual_director_decision.visual_metaphor: Evidence boundary expanding through future validation.
visual_director_decision.focus_decision: Contribution at the centre, bounded by what is not yet proven.
visual_director_decision.layout_boundary: Keep the distinction between achieved and future explicit.

graphic_language_hint.suggested_graphic_language: Contribution-to-validation roadmap with explicit evidence boundary
